summary: John Taber is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He earned his D.Phil. at the University of Hamburg (1973–1979) under Lambert Schmithausen, Reiner Wiehl, Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan, and Albrecht Wezler. He taught at Case Western Reserve University (~1984–1989) and the University of New Mexico (~1989).

John Thompson Platts was an Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics scholar educated at Bedford School and Balliol College, Oxford. He taught at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1858–1859, 1861) and served as Teacher of Persian at the University of Oxford (1880).

John Vincent Bellezza is a scholar of Tibetology and history and archaeology. He studied under Yungdrung Tenzin and Tshering Choephel, and he held an affiliation with the Tibetan Academy of Social Sciences, attested in 2014.

John W. Pettit is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He completed undergraduate studies at Haverford College and doctoral work under Robert A. F. Thurman, also studying under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Lal Mani Joshi, Gunapala Dharmasiri, and Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa.

John W. Schroeder is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Oregon under Don Levi. He taught at the University of Oregon (1993–1994), the College of Wooster (1994–1995), and St. Mary's College of Maryland (1996).

John W. Spellman was a scholar of Indology and history and archaeology. He held posts at the University of Washington (~1964–1967) and the University of Windsor, where he served as a professor (~1967–1999).

John Wilson was an Indology, linguistics, and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Edinburgh (1819–1828). He served as President of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (~1837–1842) and Vice-Chancellor of the University of Mumbai (1869).

Join Saeki was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Sennyu-ji under Jōchō Chihaya. He held posts at Kangakuin, the University of Tokyo, the Japan Academy (1929), and served as head priest at Horyu-ji (1903–1950).

Jokai Hiraoka was a scholar of Buddhist studies, history and archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Kyoto University and the University of Tokyo (~1944–1948), later holding posts at Shuchiin University and as a professor at Otemae University (~1966, attested 1987).

Jon Kabat-Zinn is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his Ph.D. at MIT (~1964–1971) under Salvador E. Luria. He held posts at the Insight Meditation Society, the Stress Reduction Clinic (~1979–1995), and the University of Massachusetts Chan Medical School (~1979–2000).

Jonardon Ganeri is a philosopher and Indologist who studied at Cambridge and Oxford, completing a D.Phil. under Bimal Krishna Matilal. He held posts at Nottingham, Liverpool, Sussex, Monash, New York University (~2013–2020), and the University of Toronto (~2020).

Jonathan A. Silk is a Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology scholar who earned his doctorate at the University of Michigan under Luis O. Gómez. He held faculty posts at Western Michigan University (~1995–1998), Yale University (1998–2002), and UCLA (~2002–2007).

Jonathan C. Gold is a scholar in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He taught at the University of Vermont, Drew University (attested 2006), and Princeton University (attested 2015–2016).

Jonathan Christopher Cleary was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed doctoral studies at Harvard University (~1974–1982) under Masatoshi Nagatomi and worked as an instructor at Wesleyan University.
Jonathan Edwards was a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Yale University (~1716–1722) and later held posts at Yale University (~1724–1726) and Princeton University (~1758).

Jonathan Geen is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned his doctorate at McMaster University in 2001 under Phyllis Granoff. He has held teaching posts at McMaster University, Butler University, and the University of Rochester.

Jonathan Glover is a philosopher who studied at Tonbridge School and Corpus Christi College, Oxford (~1960–1964). He held posts as a fellow and tutor at New College (~1967–1998) and later served at King's College London (~1998–2013).

Jonathan Lear is a philosopher who studied at Yale, Cambridge, and Rockefeller University (Ph.D. ~1973–1978). He held academic posts at Yale (1978–1996), the University of Cambridge and Clare College (1979–1989), and the University of Chicago (2014–2022).

Jonathan Mark Kenoyer is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Woodstock School and the University of California, Berkeley (~1970–1983), he has held a professorship in anthropology at the University of Wisconsin-Madison since approximately 1985.

Jonathan Z. Smith was a religious studies scholar who studied at Haverford College and Yale University (~1960–1969). He held posts at Dartmouth College (~1965–1966), UC Santa Barbara (~1966–1968), and the University of Chicago (1977–1982).
